Article (plain text of the PDF):

Rational Linear Relations and Laplace Equations for Dihedral
Modular Graph Functions up to Weight 11
Noah Schittenhelm
Hack-Nation 2026, Team Ninja Turtles

Preprint, October 4, 2026
Abstract
Two-loop dihedral modular graph functions C(a, b, c) arise in the low-energy expansion
of the one-loop closed-string amplitude. We ask how many independent rational linear
relations hold among C(a, b, c), E(w) and ζ(w) at odd weight w. A counting of linearly
independent modular graph forms exists and predicts higher weights [1]. We find numerically
that the relation space has dimension exactly 1 at weights 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11. The weight-9
relation is 960E(9) + ζ(9) − 2160C(4, 4, 1) − 4320C(4, 3, 2) − 960C(3, 3, 3) = 0. We also
verify inhomogeneous Laplace equations for C(3, 1, 1), C(2, 1, 1) and C(2, 2, 1). Holomorphic
identities and an eta-quotient span table for N ≤ 30 are certified exactly. The method
is 32-digit evaluation at verifier-chosen points, an exact leading Laurent coefficient, and a
singular-value gap for completeness. All modular-graph-function statements are numerical
observations, not proofs, and are checked at 4 points only.
Keywords: modular graph functions, Eisenstein series, string theory one-loop amplitude,
Laplace equation, linear relations, low-energy expansion

Noah (noah@schittenhelm.dev), Version 2

1

Introduction

Modular graph functions are lattice sums over p = mτ + n. They arise as coefficients of the
low-energy expansion of the one-loop closed-string amplitude. Identities among them were proved
for weights below six [2], and all weight-six identities and all dihedral weight-seven identities were
obtained and proven [3]. They satisfy Laplace eigenvalue equations with inhomogeneous terms
polynomial in non-holomorphic Eisenstein series [4]. A counting of linearly independent modular
graph forms confirms partial results and gives predictions for higher, hitherto unexplored weights
[1]. Basis decompositions of two- and three-point modular graph forms are available [5].
The open question is the exact relation space among C(a, b, c), E(w) and ζ(w) at weights 9
and 11, together with explicit relations.
Contribution. We determine the relation space numerically at the odd weights 3, 5, 7, 9
and 11, with an explicit relation at each. We verify Laplace equations for three functions. We
certify holomorphic string-theory identities exactly by Sturm bounds.
Summary of results.
• The weight-3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 observations show a relation space of dimension exactly 1 at
each weight.
• The explicit weight-9 relation has an inconclusive literature status [1].
• The weight-11 relation was not found in a targeted literature search.
• The Laplace observations give eigenvalue equations with Eisenstein and zeta sources.
• The propositions on holomorphic identities (Jacobi, θE8 , θD16 , ∆, j) are exact Sturm-bound
certificates.
• The eta-quotient span table for N ≤ 30 is exact and exhaustive.

Model and assumptions

All parameters are fixed in.
• Holomorphic expansion variable: q = e2πiτ . Eisenstein series are normalised by a0 = 1,

• Lattice-sum normalisation of E(s) and C(a, b, c): factors τ2 /(π|mτ + n|2 ) .
• The weight of C(a, b, c) is w = a + b + c. ζ(k) is the Riemann zeta function, a constant.
• Laplacian: L = τ22 (∂τ21 + ∂τ22 ), evaluated by a fourth-order finite-difference scheme with step

• Verifier points: 4 points, seed 4711, |τ1 | ≤ 1/2, 1 ≤ τ2 ≤ 2.5.
• Working precision: 32 digits.
• Tolerance: maximal relative residual 1e-24 (1e-14 with Laplacian).
• Completeness is tested on normalised value matrices at points with seed 4712.

3

Method

Certificates.
The eta-span table is exact and exhaustive. - Per relation. Each modular-graph-function
relation is checked by the exact leading Laurent coefficient and numerically at the verifier points
to 32 digits. - Completeness. The dimension of the relation space is read off from a singular-value
gap of the normalised value matrix. Singular values below 1e-24 count as kernel, and those above
1e-8 count as non-kernel. - Laplace equations. These are checked by finite differences at tolerance
1e-14.
Trusted base. The Sturm-bound coefficient comparison is exact. The modular-graphfunction evaluation, the finite-difference Laplacian and the singular-value decomposition are
floating-point computations. Relations among modular graph functions are therefore numerical
observations at the verifier points, not theorems.
Basis origin. The weight-11 hypothesis basis came from a human-guided exploration and
was then verified by the code verifier.
Execution. The work was carried out by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory in which
every statement is accepted only after code verification. Details are in Appendix A.

7

Discussion, limitations and open questions

All modular-graph-function statements are numerical observations at 4 verifier points. None is a
theorem. Residuals far below the tolerance 1e-24, the exact leading Laurent coefficient and the
singular-value gaps make accidental relations unlikely, but they do not prove an identity. The
weight-6 case remains undecided. The literature status of the weight-9 relation is inconclusive,
and it may be implied by the counting of [1]. No weight-11 relation was found in the targeted
search.
Open questions:
(i) Prove the weight-9 and weight-11 relations.
(ii) Decide the weight-6 relation space with a basis and precision that meet the gap criterion.
(iii) Find a feasible route to the full ten-function weight-11 basis.
(iv) Determine the relation space at weights beyond those studied here [1].

A

Agentic laboratory

Workflow. The laboratory ran 8 rounds with 24 verified statements and 3 negative results.
Every round was preregistered before the experiment (prereg.md). Several agents with distinct
roles attempted each question (labelled sparsam, numeriker, skeptiker, theoretiker in the run
record). Only code-verified claims were kept.
Red team. The adversarial counter-checks numbered 30 in total: 2 passed, 27 did not pass,
and 1 was not executable. Typical variants altered a coefficient, for example the ζ(5) source
term, and were refuted exactly or by large residuals.
Novelty search. Targeted searches ran per result over varying numbers of abstracts.
Negative results, detail. At weight 6, the attempts that submitted a check returned no
confirmed relation, with smallest large singular value 2.44e-8. The first weight-11 attempt used a
cascade that was aborted.
